pages.text: Julia is six. She is in her backyard, playing on her scooter.
pages.picture: Julia riding her red scooter across the lawn, happy, hair bouncing

pages.text: Then she hears a yelp. "Yelp! Yelp!" It is from the woods.
pages.picture: Julia stopped on her red scooter, one hand cupped to her ear, listening, looking toward the wooden garden gate and the woods beyond it

pages.text: Julia hops up on the gate and jumps down. Then she runs to the woods.
pages.picture: Julia climbing over the wooden garden gate and jumping down the other side, running toward the trees; her red scooter left lying on the lawn behind her

pages.text: Under a tree sits a dragon. He is white, and his scales shine pink and green and blue.
pages.picture: Toby alone, sitting curled up under the big oak in the clearing, small and sad, his white scales shining with pink, green and blue sparkles; seen as if Julia has just come through the ferns

pages.text: The dragon looks up. A big tear drips down his nose.
pages.picture: close-up of Toby under the big oak, looking up, a big tear dripping down his nose

pages.text: "I am Toby," he said. "I ran away from home."
pages.picture: Toby sitting under the big oak, shy, still a bit teary, telling Julia his name; Julia crouching in front of him, kind and curious

pages.text: "Is your home far?" asked Julia. "It is a cave on top of Super-Tall Peak," said Toby.
pages.picture: Toby pointing one claw far away through a gap in the trees; on the horizon stands Super-Tall Peak, a very tall, thin, pointy grey mountain much taller than the hills around it, with a dark cave mouth near the very top; Julia looking where he points

pages.text: "But what made you run away?" asked Julia. Toby looks down at his feet. He will not say.
pages.picture: under the big oak: Toby looking down at his feet, keeping a secret; Julia beside him, head tilted, curious

pages.text: Julia pats his nose. "You can stay with me," she said. "I have a play house!"
pages.picture: under the big oak: Julia gently patting Toby's nose, smiling; Toby comforted, eyes half closed

pages.text: Toby squeezes into the play house. He just fits. "Hush!" said Julia. "Mom must not see you."
pages.picture: Toby squeezed inside the little playhouse, he only just fits, wings squashed, peeking out of the door; Julia beside it with a finger to her lips, glancing back at the back door of the house
